problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,0]\times [-2,0]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}xy-1 \\ {y}^{3}+3x{y}^{4}+3\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts with ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,-1]^{T}.$ Round your answer to three decimal places (if needed).

feedback.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [1,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-6 \\ {x}^{3}-3xy+4\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate one iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts with ${x}_{0}=[1,\,2]^{T}.$ Round your answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{1}≈[$ | {{field-1}} | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-6) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-6) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}-3xy+4) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}-3xy+4)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x & 3{y}^{2} \\ 3{x}^{2}-3y & -3x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & 3{y}^{2} \\ 3{x}^{2}-3y & -3x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-6 \\ {x}^{3}-3xy+4\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}-{[\begin{aligned}2x & 3{y}^{2} \\ 3{x}^{2}-3y & -3x\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-6 \\ {x}^{3}-3xy+4\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(1) & 3(2)^{2} \\ 3(1)^{2}-3(2) & -3(1)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(1)^{2}+(2)^{3}-6 \\ (1)^{3}-3(1)(2)+4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2 & 12 \\ -3 & -3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{2\cdot (-3)-12\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}-3 & -12 \\ 3 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{30}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{10} \\ \frac{53}{30}\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.9 \\ 1.767\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
